rule: Byte and count budgets set their limit at most 20 percent above the measured baseline, so a 20 percent regression fails CI. Time budgets run on shared hosted runners with software rendering, so each declares a headroom factor of at most 3 and a reason, takes the fastest of several samples and asserts at one RTT only. Manual budgets are measured by hand and recorded as result files. See docs/adr/0154-performance-budget-file-and-regression-rule.md.

budgets.measures: The longest main thread long task entry during a four tile auto region pass on the fake model, with the tile resampling and the AIS post-processing in a worker and the document write as a React transition, the fastest of three passes in one test as ADR 0154 asks for time budgets. The baseline is the largest 4 ms timer gap of the unthrottled passes of two M4 runs of the spec, 16.3 ms, rounded up, and no pass had a long task, so it bounds the longest task from above
budgets.headroomReason: A hosted runner with software rendering is slower than the Apple M4 baseline of 17 ms, but on CI run 42622593110 its three unthrottled passes reported no long task at all and a largest timer gap of 22.8 to 39.5 ms, so 51 ms holds there. Resampling a tile on the main thread took 221 ms with the CPU slowed four times and tile post-processing about 120 ms, so moving either back off the worker still fails.
budgets.environment: Chrome headless against the Vite dev server with the fake model and fake slide reader, 1280 x 720

budgets.measures: The longest main thread long task entry during a four tile auto region pass on the fake model with the CPU slowed four times through the Chrome DevTools Protocol, the fastest of three passes in one test as ADR 0154 asks for time budgets. The baseline is the faster of the two throttled passes on the hosted runner in CI run 42622593110, 63 ms with 3 long tasks, the other being 73 ms with 9. The Apple M4 reports no long task at this throttle
budgets.headroomReason: The hosted runner renders in software and is already several times slower than the M4 before the throttle, so the 50 ms long task line the M4 holds cannot hold there. Twice the runner baseline still fails the regression this guards, since resampling on the main thread gave a 152 ms longest task on the M4 at the same throttle and would be longer on the runner.
budgets.environment: Chrome headless on a GitHub hosted ubuntu runner against the Vite dev server with the fake model and fake slide reader, 1280 x 720, CPU throttled four times

budgets.measures: One POST of 10,000 cell annotations to the bulk annotation endpoint, from the request to the 201, one sample
budgets.headroomReason: The baseline is the whole test call on the last green hosted run, so it is an upper bound of the request. On a busy hosted runner, where the whole db job ran 1.43 times slower, the request alone took 6488 ms, 1.8 times the baseline, with no change in its path. The test keeps one 10,000 row sample because three would triple it, so 2.5 times covers a busy runner and still fails a doubling on a quiet one.
budgets.environment: GitHub hosted ubuntu runner, PostGIS 17 service container, FastAPI test client in process, so no network RTT
budgets.todo: Take the request time from a few green hosted runs and tighten the baseline to it.

budgets.measures: 95th percentile of one hover hit test over 1,000,000 nuclei with two of eight groups hidden or locked, fastest of three passes
budgets.headroomReason: The work is a few hundred array reads, so a slower or loaded hosted CPU scales it linearly. Three times covers that while the product bound of 1 ms stays asserted in the same test.
